tickets.title: P3-128: a copier with every relationship switched OFF reports '[ COPIER LIVE - SIM ONLY ]' and says copies reach simulation followers -- nothing is copied at all
tickets.defect:
MEASURED ON THE LIVE BOX 2026-08-16, seconds after P1-125 put this sentence onto the operator's browser page:

    headline: "[ COPIER LIVE - SIM ONLY ]"
    detail:   "2 relationships, 0 enabled. Nothing is armed for live, so copies reach
               simulation followers only and a live follower is refused."

Both relationships were DISABLED. Nothing reached a simulation follower, or any other kind. The detail line even carries the contradicting number -- "0 enabled" -- in its own first clause.

`CopierStatusView.Headline` tests, in order: unrecognised mode > not acting > total == 0 > all quarantined > some quarantined > armed == 0 > armed. There is NO RUNG FOR `enabled == 0`, so a copier whose relationships are all switched off falls into the `armed == 0` rung, whose sentence was written for a different state -- relationships that ARE enabled but are not armed for live.

This is P3-122 in a second class, filed the day P3-122 was closed: a sentence that is true of a NEIGHBOURING state, describing behaviour that is not happening, in the direction that reassures.
tickets.spec:
ONE FILE, ONE METHOD: the `Headline` ladder in `addons/CopierStatusView.cs`.

ADD ONE RUNG, for a copier that has relationships or group followers but has none of them switched on:

  * CONDITION: `total > 0 && enabled == 0`.
  * TEXT: must contain `NOTHING ENABLED` (the existing bracket style, e.g. `[ COPIER LIVE - NOTHING ENABLED ]`).
  * SEVERITY: `CopierStatusSeverity.Warn`. NOT Info. A copier holding relationships it is not running is 'configured to do something it is not doing', which is Warn's own stated definition, and Info renders in the same grey as a healthy copier.
  * DETAIL: must NOT contain the word 'simulation' in any case. It must state the true situation -- every relationship is switched off, so nothing is copied -- and must keep folding its numbers out of the same `counts` string the other rungs use, so the count cannot drift from the list it describes.

WHERE THE RUNG GOES, AND THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART:

  * BELOW both quarantine rungs. `quarantined >= enabled` is `1 >= 0` for a copier that is all-quarantined AND all-disabled, so a rung placed above them would swallow the quarantine report -- and quarantine ranks first deliberately, because it is the one state the operator did not choose.
  * ABOVE the `armed == 0` rung, which is the rung currently answering this state wrongly.
  * Do NOT touch the `total == 0` rung above it. 'No relationships at all' and 'relationships that are all switched off' are different answers and both are already distinguished elsewhere in this file.

DO NOT CHANGE `Describe`. It already folds `enabled` out of BOTH the relationship list and the group list (`if (g.IsEnabled) enabled += followers;`), which is why the group case is covered by the same rung. A fix that reads only the relationship list fails the group acceptance test.

DO NOT CHANGE any other rung's text, severity or order. Five of the assertions in this file's existing P1-121 tests pin them.
tickets.context:
SCOPE. This is a display-only class: it decides what the WPF window and (since P1-125) the browser UI SAY about the copier, and it decides nothing about what the copier DOES. No copy path, no gate, no engine state. `TradeCopierEngine.IsCopierActingMode` and `IsRecognisedCopierMode` stay the sole owners of what a mode means -- `IsActing` delegates to the engine and must keep doing so. A literal mode comparison introduced anywhere in this file is the defect P1-121's own header warns about.

THE NEGATIVE CONTROL IS ALREADY IN THE SUITE AND IS GREEN NOW. It must STAY green: an ENABLED relationship that is not armed for live still reads `SIM ONLY` and still says 'simulation' in its detail, because that state really does copy to simulation followers only. A headline that said NOTHING ENABLED whenever nothing is ARMED satisfies every red assertion in this ticket and destroys the rung it is imitating. `enabled` and `armed` are different counters and the whole ticket is that they were conflated.

Severity ordering matters to two consumers: the window maps it to a brush, and the browser page maps it to a CSS class where `warn` is amber and `info` is the same grey as healthy. Reporting this state as Info is how it stayed unnoticed on a page built to make a non-acting copier visible without being looked for.
expect_green: P3-128: a copier with NOTHING enabled does not claim copies reach simulation followers
P3-128: and the headline does not read SIM ONLY
P3-128: it names what is actually true -- nothing is enabled
P3-128: and a switched-off group does not copy to simulation followers
P3-128: it reads as nothing enabled, from the group's own IsEnabled
tickets.note_expect_green:
All six were VERIFIED RED at the 2012 passed / 6 failed baseline, by running the suite before this ticket was written -- expect_green is matched against the runner's FAILURE LINES and means red-now-green-after. The observed failure output reproduced the LIVE payload verbatim, which is why these are the right six.

FIVE MORE ASSERTIONS IN THE SAME TWO TESTS ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT FROM THIS LIST, because they are GREEN NOW and must STAY green. Each one refuses a specific wrong fix, and a wrong fix passes all six listed above:

  * an ENABLED, unarmed relationship still reads SIM ONLY, and still says 'simulation' in its detail -- the negative control. A rung keyed on `armed == 0` instead of `enabled == 0` satisfies every listed assertion and deletes the state being imitated.
  * one enabled relationship out of two is NOT 'nothing enabled' -- a rung keyed on 'any relationship disabled' passes the listed six as well.
  * an all-quarantined, all-disabled copier still reports its QUARANTINE -- this is what fails if the new rung is placed above the quarantine rungs, and it is the specific ordering hazard the spec names.
  * a group with two followers is not 'NOTHING CONFIGURED' -- the rung above must keep its meaning.
  * the relationship count is still present in the detail -- the numbers stay folded out of the collections rather than tracked beside them (F-9).

A detector needs a negative test: a headline that reported NOTHING ENABLED for everything would pass all six red assertions.

regions.note: The whole private Headline method, including its doc comment's meaning: the rungs are ordered by what BINDS. Emit the method complete, with the new rung inserted between the quarantine rungs and the `armed == 0` rung. Every other rung must come back byte-identical in text and severity.
